274K likes, 859 comments - nasawebb on October 6, 2026: "Brewing up new stars 🪄
 
@NASAWebb’s unique view of the stellar nursery known as NGC 7129 reveals numerous stars formerly hidden in this cosmic cauldron. 
 
Stars begin their life in cold, dense regions of dust and gas, hiding from view of most telescopes. Webb’s high degree of infrared sensitivity allows astronomers to peer through dust to study these baby stars. 
 
In this image, we can see stars in various stages of development. The most mature and massive (about 5-8x the mass of our Sun) is the region’s bright central star. In the cavity on the left, appearing in gold, is the largest demonstration of its impact. The outflows from an earlier stage in the star’s development carve into the dense molecular cloud of hydrogen, and combine with the star’s light, causing it to glow. 
 
The region on the right, represented in red, hides much younger objects than those on the left: protostars. As the protostars accumulate matter and increase mass, they eject outflows of super heated material that interact with matter around the star, creating shocks that cause the textured appearance we see in this image. More protostar outflows are at upper left where a dark shadow is being cast by a protostar disk, visible against the surrounding nebula, depicted in blue. 
 
Seeing these different structures help astronomers study the star lifecycle in various stages, leading to a more complete understanding of our universe. 

See more in the link in @NASAWebb’s bio.
 
Image credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Processing: Alyssa Pagan.
 
Image description in comments.".

1M likes, 5,306 comments - nasa on October 2, 2026: "Swipe for countless stars

Sagittarius B2 is the most massive and most active star-forming region in the Milky Way. It produces half of the stars in our home galaxy’s core.

This image of Sagittarius B2 was taken by our @NASAWebb telescope.

#NASA #Space #Stars".

28K likes, 200 comments - nasa on October 22, 2026: "Creepy crawly crater 🕷️
 
The Spider Crater in Australia, the product of a meteorite impact followed by hundreds of millions of years of erosion, could cause a fright! Its “legs” are sandstone ridges that stayed while other rocks were worn away.
 
#NASA #Earth #Spider".

214K likes, 772 comments - nasa on October 21, 2026: "Ahh… blue lagoon 🏖️
 
This deep-blue sea of gas and dust—called Messier 8 or the Lagoon Nebula—is a hotbed of star formation. The young stars within the nebula emit rays of high-energy light, including X-rays shown in pink by @nasachandraxray.
 
#NASA #Messier #Spongebob".

200K likes, 656 comments - nasa on October 15, 2026: "Objects in mirror are farther than they appear 🪞⁣

The golden galaxies (center) in this image are in the foreground, but the orange ones bunched together (left) are much farther away. The nearer galaxies bend light, causing this optical illusion.".

This photo of Egypt’s Nile River was taken aboard the @ISS as it soared above Earth. The river sparkles with city lights, highlighting where people live along the waterways.

#Astrophotography #Earth #Egypt".

#NASA #Launch #Jellyfish".
